calendar.impact: The December WTI contract expires Friday, closing the contract the front differential was marked against all month, with December WCS already rolled off the settlements file.
calendar.title: December WTI expiry

calendar.impact: Shareholders vote on the plan of arrangement under which Cenovus acquires Athabasca, with closing expected in December.
calendar.title: Athabasca special meeting on the Cenovus arrangement

calendar.impact: The wider group meets to set the 2027 production framework, with the IEA printing October supply above demand and the official US inventory report confirming builds.
calendar.title: OPEC+ ministerial meeting on the 2027 framework

changes.balance: The surplus has moved from forecast to confirmed stock build, while the basin balance keeps tanking toward December storage of 76.24 million barrels against 80.6 million of working capacity and the December apportionment percentages remain unread in public sources.
changes.body: Brent Jan27 settled $91.95, down $1.19, and WTI Dec26 settled $83.26, down $2.75, on Wednesday (Reuters, Nov 18), and Asia held Brent $92.00 and WTI $83.00 at 0455 GMT on Thursday (Reuters, Nov 19). The Brent to WTI spread closed at $8.69, the widest in about two weeks. The EIA report for the week ending Nov 13 printed crude up 3.380 million barrels to 417.797 million, gasoline up 5.129 million, distillate up 1.571 million, utilisation at 95.7 percent and the strategic reserve down 3.174 million to 276.361 million, its lowest since August 1982.
changes.conditional: A second consecutive confirmed build of this size extends the surplus pricing into the winter strip; a draw next week on the same utilisation would reopen whether Wednesday was positioning rather than information.
changes.delta: Brent settled down 1.3 percent and WTI down 3.2 percent at its lowest since August 26, Asia held the level, and the official report printed crude up 3.380 million against surveys of 1.0 and 0.058 million
changes.source: Reuters, Nov 18 and 19, 2026; EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report, released Nov 18, 2026
changes.title: WTI took the repricing, the inventory build confirmed, and the spread widened to $8.69
changes.vintage: Reuters settles, Nov 18, 2026, and overnight tape at 0455 GMT, Nov 19, 2026

changes.balance: December's space allocation and tank build now point the same way: apportionment rose on both lines into a month tanking to 76.24 million barrels against 80.6 million of working capacity, and the traded strip has to digest a harder notice than it tightened against.
changes.body: December Mainline apportionment is Light 24 percent and Heavy 17 percent at Kerrobert (Enbridge notice, announced Nov 18), up from November's Light 19 percent and Heavy 7 percent (Enbridge notice, Oct 20). The Cromer and Superior points for December were not in the report received. December WCS has rolled off the settlements file; January WCS settled -$23.45 (ICE TMW settle, Nov 18) on one lot, with February at -$22.55 on 530 lots and the traded strip tightening again into the notice.
changes.conditional: A traded strip that holds its tightening against a 24 and 17 notice says the winter is priced; a strip that gives the tightening back reopens the widening path for the front.
changes.delta: December Mainline apportionment is Light 24 percent and Heavy 17 percent at Kerrobert (Enbridge notice, announced Nov 18), up from November's 19 and 7 percent, landing in a month whose implied storage reaches 76.24 million barrels
changes.source: Enbridge apportionment notice, announced Nov 18, 2026; ICE Report Center EOD, Nov 18, 2026
changes.title: December apportionment printed 24 percent light and 17 percent heavy, above November on both lines

changes.balance: The strait's risk pricing is being set by the least reliable gauge set of the autumn: if the tracker gauge is right, the surplus pricing is missing roughly half the strait's pre-war flow; if the wire narrative is right, the incident tempo is not removing barrels.
changes.body: The Tara Gas, attacked north of Khasab on Tuesday, is now reported with one seafarer missing and eleven injured. Iran's Nov 18 claim of three tankers disabled by mines is unconfirmed with no vessel named. The JMIC threat level remains SEVERE on its Nov 12 update. The US and Iran exchanged fire again, Iran targeted US installations in Kuwait, and the Houthis fired toward Riyadh on Thursday. Kpler's latest measured clearance, to Nov 11, is 8,264 kb/d, 48 percent of pre-war, and is now eight days old.
changes.conditional: A fresh measured clearance print near the Kpler level reprices the front against the surplus; a measured print near pre-war levels confirms the surplus is in charge and the incident tempo is noise for supply.
changes.delta: Reuters described Hormuz shipments as back to roughly pre-war levels on Nov 18 while the latest measured clearance, Kpler to Nov 11, stands at 48 percent of pre-war, and no fresher measured print has been published
changes.source: Reuters, Nov 18 to 19, 2026; Kpler briefing, Nov 13, 2026; JMIC update, Nov 12, 2026
changes.title: The flow gauges disagree: wire reporting says pre-war, the tracker gauge says 48 percent
changes.vintage: Kpler briefing, Nov 13, 2026, data to Nov 11

flags.body: December Mainline apportionment (Light 24 percent at Kerrobert, Heavy 17 percent at Kerrobert) is announced for December, up from November's Light 19 percent and Heavy 7 percent. The Cromer and Superior points for December were not in the report received. The evidence pack includes the balance build with supply running about 200 kb/d a month above the proven 4,541.6 kb/d egress bound into tanks, December implied storage of 76.24 million barrels against 80.6 million of working capacity, and a January front differential that traded one lot.
flags.title: December apportionment: Light 24 and Heavy 17 at Kerrobert, up from 19 and 7 in November
flags.trigger: The Enbridge December apportionment percentages as published in the notice itself

flags.body: Two tanker incidents are confirmed in the current cycle, the Tara Gas among them with one seafarer missing and eleven injured. Iranian claims of three tankers disabled by mines on Nov 18 carry no named vessel and no confirmation. Kpler's latest measured clearance is 8,264 kb/d to Nov 11, 48 percent of pre-war, and is now eight days old, while wire reporting on Nov 18 described shipments at roughly pre-war levels. A confirmed measured flow print resolves which gauge the pricing should follow.
flags.title: Flow gauges in open disagreement: clearance 8,264 kb/d to Nov 11 against wire reporting of pre-war levels
flags.trigger: A fresh measured clearance print from a tracker, or confirmation of a loadings halt from an owner or UKMTO product

flags.body: Reuters reporting from two industry sources puts Russian refining processing down about 45 percent point to point since late October, with 15 of 35 major refineries disrupted, while average November processing is only 5 to 10 percent below September and October. The two figures measure different things, and the monthly average is the one that prices product supply. Ilsky and Afipsky were struck again on Nov 17 and overnight Nov 18 with damage not independently verified.
flags.title: Russian processing: 45 percent point to point, 5 to 10 percent on the month
flags.trigger: A monthly Russian processing figure for November, or verified damage assessments for the Ilsky and Afipsky strikes
